# progress — unified-anoa-binary-terminal-cdp

## task-001 — terminal options on the shared config parser (2026-07-31)

- **Nothing compiles in this sandbox, confirmed.** No `cmake`, no Qt6 headers,
  no `qmake6`, and `apt-get install qt6-base-dev cmake` fails (packages not
  available). Only `g++` and `make` exist. The plan's "every phase is a CI
  round-trip" is literal.
- **Cheap local signal that does work:** syntax-check a Qt source against
  hand-written stub headers —
  `g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only -I<stubdir> -include <stubdir>/qtstub.h src/config/config.cpp`
  with one header defining QString/QStringList/QTextStream/QUrl/
  QCommandLineParser/QCommandLineOption/QJson*/QSettings/QFileInfo, plus empty
  forwarding headers named `QCommandLineParser`, `QUrl`, … This catches typos,
  wrong overloads and undeclared identifiers before burning a CI run.
  `config.cpp` is a good candidate because it only touches QtCore. Stub gotcha:
  QStringList needs `begin()`/`end()` or the existing range-for over
  `extensionPaths` fails to compile.
- **Keep string literals in `src/` ASCII-only.** An em dash in a `QTextStream`
  error message was the only non-ASCII string literal anywhere in `src/*.cpp` —
  this binary also builds on MSVC, so it was replaced. Non-ASCII in *comments*
  is common in this repo and fine.
- `QCommandLineParser::process()` only hard-exits on unknown *options*;
  unregistered *positional* args are collected silently. So the `terminal`
  positional needs no parser registration — but every terminal flag does, which
  is why this task came first.
- **`--fps` default is 30 here, not anoa-term's 10.** The task spec said 30; the
  standalone tool shipped 10. Phase 2's port must not assume parity on that
  number — decide deliberately rather than copying either side.
- Terminal fields live in `Config` with in-struct defaults and come *only* from
  the CLI; `loadConfigFile()` is untouched by design. `parseArgs()` never
  touches `terminalMode` — the argv pre-scan in `main.cpp` owns that field
  (task-002).
- `tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt` builds `anoa-config-lib` from
  `src/config/config.cpp` alone against `Qt6::Core` only. `QUrl` is QtCore, so
  the `--cdp` validation adds no link dependency. Anything needing
  QtNetwork/QtGui must stay out of config.cpp.

## task-002 — argv pre-scan dispatch + runTerminal() branch (2026-07-31)

- **The `--headless` scan lost its `break`.** It could stop early before because
  it looked for one thing; now the same loop also hunts `terminal`, so it must
  run to the end. `qputenv` is idempotent, so a repeated `--headless` is
  harmless — but do not re-add a `break` there.
- **argv surgery pattern that works:** shift left from the match, then
  `argv[--argc] = nullptr` to keep the array null-terminated (QCoreApplication
  expects `argv[argc] == nullptr`), then `--i` so the loop re-examines the
  argument shifted into the current slot. Verified against 9 argv shapes with a
  standalone harness (`g++` on a verbatim copy of the loop) — including
  adjacent `terminal terminal` and `--headless` on either side.
- **Known misparse, accepted deliberately:** the raw scan has no option-arity
  knowledge, so `--profile-name terminal` is eaten as the subcommand. Same class
  of limitation the `--headless` scan already had. Teaching main.cpp the option
  table would duplicate the parser it invokes three lines later. If this ever
  bites, the fix is "only argv[1] counts as the subcommand", not an option list.
- **Extending the stub-header trick from task-001 to main.cpp:** quoted includes
  resolve relative to the *including file's* directory, so `-I<stubdir>` cannot
  shadow `src/browser/anoa_browser.h` while compiling `src/main.cpp`. Copy
  main.cpp into the stub dir and compile it there — then `browser/`, `cdp/`,
  `http/` resolve to stubs while `config/` and `terminal/` still resolve to the
  real headers via `-Isrc`. Both `-DQ_OS_WIN` and POSIX paths syntax-check clean
  under `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`.
- **Verify the Windows compile-out negatively, not just positively:** `g++ -E
  -DQ_OS_WIN ... | grep -c runTerminal` must be 0. A plain `-fsyntax-only` pass
  proves nothing — `-Isrc` would happily find the header even if the `#ifndef`
  guard were wrong.
- `Q_OS_WIN` comes from `<QtGlobal>`; it is included explicitly at the top of
  main.cpp rather than relied on transitively via `<QApplication>`, because the
  `#ifndef Q_OS_WIN` guard around the terminal include sits above any Qt use.
- `runTerminal()` is a **stub** (prints resolved target, returns 0) and
  `terminal_app.{h,cpp}` intentionally has no Qt class in the header — only a
  forward-declared `struct Config`. Phase 2 replaces the body.
- `anoa-term` target and its `install(TARGETS)` are still in CMakeLists.txt;
  task-007 owns their removal. The new POSIX-guarded `target_sources` block sits
  directly after the main `target_sources` call.

## task-003 — unit tests for the terminal config surface (2026-07-31)

- **`parseArgs` cannot be tested in-process.** It reads argv back off
  `QCoreApplication::instance()` (not its own `argc/argv` — both parameters are
  unnamed/unused) and validates with `::exit(1)`. A QTest binary already owns a
  QCoreApplication, so every parseArgs assertion goes through the existing
  self-reinvocation trick: `ANOA_TEST_HARNESS=parse_args` + flags as QProcess
  args, harness prints the resulting Config as one compact JSON line on stdout,
  test parses it. Valid and invalid cases share one helper (`runParseArgs`) —
  exit code plus parsed fields.
- `runParseArgs` returns `exitCode = -1` on timeout or crash rather than
  `proc.exitCode()`, which is meaningless after a CrashExit. A `QVERIFY(exitCode
  != 0)` would otherwise pass on a segfault.
- **`QJsonObject::operator[]` on a non-const object inserts a null value for a
  missing key**, so a typo'd key reads back as `""`/`0` instead of failing at
  lookup. The default-value assertions (fps 30, termPort 9222, termHost
  127.0.0.1) are what actually catch a missing key here.
- **The QCoreApplication/QImage assumption is now a test, not a comment.**
  `TERM-GUI-01..03` assert `metaObject()->className() == "QCoreApplication"`
  (proves no QGuiApplication/QApplication is alive), then decode, `scaled()` and
  `convertToFormat(Format_RGB888)` a 4x2 PNG embedded as base64. The className
  check matters: without it, a future switch of the test main() to QApplication
  would silently turn the decode tests into a tautology.
- `Qt6::Gui` is linked into `anoa-browser-test-config` only. `anoa-config-lib`
  stays `Qt6::Core` + `config.cpp` alone, per the plan's constraint. Linking Gui
  also switches on `QT_GUI_LIB`, which is what pulls `qtest_gui.h` into
  `<QtTest/QtTest>` so `QCOMPARE` can print a QColor.
- **CI had no macOS unit-test job at all** — `ci.yml`'s five jobs were all
  ubuntu-22.04; macOS only appears in `release.yml`. "Green on Linux and macOS"
  was unreachable without adding one, so `unit-tests` became a 2-entry matrix
  (`qt_host`/`qt_arch` per OS, `libcups2-dev` gated on `runner.os == 'Linux'`).
  It builds only the `anoa-browser-test-config` target, not the WebEngine
  binary — but note the top-level `find_package` still requires the full Qt
  component set on macOS, which is why the WebEngine modules stay in the
  install-qt step.
- **Still unverified: everything.** No cmake and no Qt6 in the sandbox, and the
  branch has no upstream, so no CI run has happened. Verification so far is the
  stub-header syntax check from task-001 extended to the test file: copy
  `test_config.cpp` into the stub dir, add an empty `test_config.moc` and an
  empty `QtTest/QtTest`, then `g++ -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -I<stubdir>
  -Isrc -include qtstub.h`. Always confirm the harness is live by re-running it
  with a deliberate typo — an over-permissive stub can compile anything.
- If the CI run shows `QImage::loadFromData` failing without a GUI application
  object, the fallback is unchanged: `QApplication` plus `qputenv("QT_QPA_
  PLATFORM", "offscreen")` from the same argv pre-scan in `src/main.cpp`.
  `src/main.cpp` was in this task's scope for exactly that and is untouched.

## task-004 — terminal UI port + FrameBackend seam (2026-07-31)

- **The stub-header trick now runs actual code, not just a syntax check.**
  `/tmp/uistub/qtstub.h` gives QString/QByteArray real `std::string` storage, so
  `terminal_ui.cpp` links against a fake FrameBackend that logs every call.
  17 assertions cover the four hard-won input behaviours plus arrows, UTF-8
  batching, split escape sequences and the click/scroll coordinate map — all
  green, and none of it needs Qt. Recipe:
  `g++ -std=c++17 -I/tmp/uistub -Isrc -include /tmp/uistub/qtstub.h harness.cpp
  src/terminal/terminal_ui.cpp`. Worth extending for task-005/006 rather than
  waiting on CI.
- **That harness immediately found a real regression the eye missed:** the
  Ctrl-C/Ctrl-Q branch of `processInput` returns before `buf.erase(0, i)`.
  Harmless in anoa-term (the caller broke out of the loop), fatal once the
  buffer became a member — a stale Ctrl-C re-triggers on every later read, so
  the very first keystroke after it quits again. Fixed with `buf.erase(0, i+1)`
  before the `return false`. This is the one deliberate behaviour divergence
  from the original.
- **The seam is asynchronous:** `requestRgbFrame`/`requestPngFrame` are answered
  by a `frameReady`/`frameFailed` signal, not a return value. A synchronous
  transport may emit before the call returns (the HTTP backend will), so
  `TerminalUi::onFrame` can run re-entrantly inside `tick()` — that is fine and
  intended. CDP could not honour a blocking `fetch()` without a nested event
  loop, which the plan rules out.
- `sendText` takes `QByteArray`, not `QString`, on purpose: a read burst can end
  mid-UTF-8-character and `QString::fromUtf8` would turn the split tail into a
  replacement character.
- `sendScroll(pageX, pageY, dy)` uses **negative coordinates to mean "pointer
  outside the page"** — anoa-term simply omitted `&x=&y=` from the query string
  in that case, and the seam has no way to express an absent argument.
- **AUTOMOC only moc's a header that has a same-named .cpp or is listed in
  `target_sources`.** `frame_backend.h` has neither a .cpp nor an implementation,
  so it is listed explicitly in the POSIX block; without that, `FrameBackend`'s
  metaobject is never generated and the link fails. This is the single build
  assumption in this task that only CI can confirm.
- Non-ASCII kept out of `src/` string literals per task-001: the em dash and
  ellipsis in the status bar are written as `\xE2\x80\x94` / `\xE2\x80\xA6`
  constants, so the bytes on the wire match anoa-term exactly.
- `--fps` is validated to 1-120 by config.cpp, so the UI does **not** re-clamp to
  anoa-term's 1-30; it only guards against a zero divisor in `framePeriodMs()`.
- The frame loop is deliberately absent — `tick()`, `feedInput()` and the three
  slots are the entry points task-006 wires to a QTimer and a QSocketNotifier.
  `terminal_app.cpp` is still the task-002 stub.

## task-005 — /render/* HTTP transport behind the seam (2026-07-31)

- **The stub-header harness now talks to a real socket.** `/tmp/httpstub` is
  `/tmp/uistub` plus `QString::number/arg/fromStdString/toUtf8` and
  `QLatin1Char`; the harness starts a loopback listener on an ephemeral port,
  serves one canned response per exchange and asserts on the raw request text.
  32 assertions cover the request line, Bearer header, Host, `Connection:
  close`, PPM/PNG parsing, viewport headers, every input endpoint, the no-token
  config and a connect failure. Recipe:
  `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -I/tmp/httpstub -Isrc -include
  /tmp/httpstub/qtstub.h -pthread harness.cpp src/terminal/render_http_client.cpp`.
  Confirmed live by mutating the scroll sign (4 FAILs). This is the strongest
  local signal found so far — it exercises the actual wire format, not syntax.
- **`FrameBackend`'s signals are ordinary member functions in the stub world**,
  so the harness defines `FrameBackend::frameReady/frameFailed/statusChanged`
  itself and records into vectors. No moc, no Qt, and the emitting code is the
  real code.
- **The cell-to-page map moved up into the UI, so this backend never calls
  `mapCellToPage`.** anoa-term's `sendClick` returned early when the mapping
  failed and `sendScroll` dropped `&x=&y=`; the equivalent here is the UI's
  `inPage` check plus the `pageX >= 0 && pageY >= 0` guard. Note `0,0` is a
  valid on-page coordinate — the guard is `>= 0`, not `> 0`.
- **Response headers are matched lowercased**, as before, so
  `X-Anoa-Viewport-Width` in any casing works; a missing header reads as 0
  because `headerInt()` reproduces what `operator[]` + `atoi("")` used to do.
- `parsePpm` writes straight into `FrameData` and the old `Frame`/
  `std::vector<unsigned char>` pair is gone; the PNG path never decodes, it only
  reads IHDR and forwards the bytes verbatim, exactly as anoa-term did.
- **Not ported, and currently unowned: the pre-flight probe** at
  `anoa_term.cpp:704-718` (`GET /render/screenshot.ppm?w=8&h=8` before raw mode,
  so "is anoa-browser running? does it need --token?" prints on a normal screen
  instead of flashing the alt screen). It belongs to whoever wires the frame
  loop (task-006). Doing it through the seam is awkward on the CDP side: the
  HTTP backend emits `frameFailed` synchronously, a WebSocket one cannot.
- The blocking client still has **no socket timeout** — a hung server wedges the
  frame timer forever. Carried over deliberately (same as anoa-term); if the Qt
  timer ever starves in CI, this is the first suspect.
- `-Wswitch` is why `buttonName()` breaks out of the switch for `Left` instead
  of returning from it — every enumerator is listed, no `default`, so adding a
  fourth button becomes a compile error rather than a silent "left".

## task-006 — select() loop -> QCoreApplication::exec() (2026-07-31)

- **The harness now runs the whole viewer, on a real pty, without Qt.**
  `/tmp/appstub/qtstub.h` is the task-005 stub plus a *working* signal/slot
  registry and a select()-based `QCoreApplication::exec()` over stub QTimer and
  QSocketNotifier. Signals are keyed by the raw bytes of their member-function
  pointer (`std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&pmf), sizeof pmf)`) —
  legal enough for non-virtual members of single-inheritance classes, which is
  every signal here. `harness.cpp` forks a child whose stdin/stdout are a pty
  slave and calls the real `runTerminal()`; the parent is single-threaded and
  services the fake `/render/*` listener and the pty master from one select()
  loop, which is also what lets it answer the XTWINOPS `ESC [ 16 t` cell-size
  query the gfx modes send at startup. 50 assertions, all green:
  `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -I/tmp/appstub -Isrc -include
  /tmp/appstub/qtstub.h -o harness harness.cpp src/terminal/terminal_app.cpp
  src/terminal/terminal_ui.cpp src/terminal/render_http_client.cpp -lutil`.
  Do not fork the parent's HTTP server onto a thread — fork() with a live
  thread risks inheriting a held malloc lock. Confirmed live by four mutations
  (fixed 1000 ms interval -> 4 FAILs, single read() instead of the drain loop
  -> 2 FAILs, probe removed -> 5 FAILs, wrong timer wiring -> FAILs).
- **Found and fixed a hard build break in task-005's code:** `connect(fd,
  ai->ai_addr, ...)` inside `RenderHttpClient::httpRequest`. That class derives
  from QObject, so unqualified lookup finds the static `QObject::connect`
  overloads and *stops* — `::connect` from `<sys/socket.h>` is never
  considered, and the whole `anoa-browser` target fails to compile against real
  Qt6. It slipped through because task-005's stub QObject had no `connect`
  member at all. Now `::connect`. **Any POSIX call whose name collides with a
  QObject member must be `::`-qualified inside a QObject subclass** — audit
  `socket`/`connect`/`bind`/`listen`/`accept` when the CDP client lands.
- `jonggrang bug --feature <id>` cannot be used from a work session in this
  repo: the global option parser at `bin/jonggrang.js:4990` swallows
  `--feature` into `WORK_FEATURE_ID` before `cmdBug` ever sees it, so with more
  than one feature present it always dies on "Multiple features found". Record
  defects in this file instead until that is fixed upstream.
- **`terminal_ui.{h,cpp}` needed no changes.** `begin()`/`tick()`/`feedInput()`
  /`end()` were already the right seam; the whole event loop is 70 lines in
  `terminal_app.cpp`. If a later task is tempted to edit terminal_ui for the
  loop's sake, check first — it is probably the app file that is wrong.
- **stdin batching is now strictly better than anoa-term's**, on purpose. Raw
  mode sets `VMIN=0/VTIME=0`, so on a tty `read()` returns 0 the moment the
  buffer is drained rather than blocking; the notifier callback loops until
  that happens and dispatches once. anoa-term did a single 512-byte read per
  select() wakeup, so a 2000-byte paste became four `/render/type` requests.
  Note the consequence: **`read() == 0` here means "drained", not EOF.** Only
  `-1` with an errno other than EINTR/EAGAIN (EIO, which is what a hung-up pty
  master gives on Linux) is treated as stdin being gone.
- **The pre-flight probe from `anoa_term.cpp:704-718` is ported and now owned by
  this file.** It is done *through the seam*: connect a temporary lambda to
  `frameFailed`, call `requestRgbFrame(8, 8)`, disconnect, and read the flag.
  A synchronous backend (HTTP) answers before the call returns and the probe
  concludes; an asynchronous one (CDP) stays silent and the probe is a no-op by
  construction, which is the correct behaviour for it — connection state
  reaches the user via `statusChanged()` instead. Silence is treated as
  success. `frame_backend.h` needed no new virtual.
- Signal latency is one frame period (33 ms at 30 fps) because `tick()` polls
  `g_quit`/`g_resized`, exactly as the plan chose. Ctrl-C is *not* on that
  path — ISIG is off, so it arrives as byte 3 through the notifier and quits
  immediately. `kill -INT` is the slow path.
- **`g_quit` is never reset.** Harmless in the real binary (one viewer per
  process), but any in-process test that calls `runTerminal()` twice will find
  the second call quits at once. The harness forks per case for this reason.
- `--cdp` currently exits 1 with "not implemented yet" rather than silently
  falling through to the `/render/*` backend. task-012 replaces that branch
  with the real backend selection.

## task-007 — delete the anoa-term target and tools/ (2026-07-31)

- **`git rm -r tools/anoa-term` also removed `tools/`** — git does not track empty
  directories, so the parent disappeared with its only file. No separate rmdir.
- **The build graph was already clean of the target apart from the two blocks.**
  Checked `CMakeLists.txt`, `tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt`, `Makefile` and
  `scripts/`: nothing else named it. `make lint` runs clang-tidy over `src` only,
  so it never pointed at `tools/`. Everything that still says `anoa-term` is
  packaging, CI or docs — `release.yml` (8 sites), both Homebrew templates,
  `resources/anoa-browser.sh:6`, `README.md` — plus prose comments in
  `src/terminal/*` that credit the original file. Phase 5/6 own those.
- **A release built from this commit would fail** at `cp build/anoa-term` in
  release.yml. That is expected between task-007 and task-013, but do not
  workflow_dispatch a release in the gap and conclude the merge is broken.
- **`make build` produces exactly one executable, verified structurally, not by
  building:** `add_executable` appears once in the top-level file, and the only
  other one (`anoa-browser-test-config`) is behind `add_subdirectory(tests/unit)`
  which `option(BUILD_TESTS)` leaves OFF for `make configure`. Only `make test`
  re-configures with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON`.
- **Balance-check trick for a CMake edit with no cmake installed:** strip `#`
  comments, then count `if/foreach/while/function/macro` against `end*` and the
  raw parens. Both must land on 0. It will not catch a bad argument, but a
  deleted `endif()` is the realistic way to break this file and it catches that.
- **The task-006 stub harness survives in `/tmp/appstub` and is the real check
  here.** Rebuilt and re-ran it after the deletion — 50/50 green, which proves
  `src/terminal/*` never depended on `anoa_term.cpp`. Recipe unchanged from
  task-006. Cheap, so re-run it after any structural edit in this phase.

## task-008 — CDP WebSocket client with response correlation (2026-07-31)

- **A fourth stub harness, and the first one with real JSON.** `/tmp/cdpstub`
  is a fresh (not derived) `qtstub.h`: a hand-written JSON parser/serializer
  behind `QJsonValue/QJsonObject/QJsonDocument`, a `QUrl`/`QUrlQuery` that can
  round-trip a query string, `QNetworkRequest`, `QElapsedTimer`, a `QHash` over
  `std::map`, and a **fake `QWebSocket` the harness drives directly** —
  `fakeConnected()/fakeDisconnected()/fakeError()/fakeReceive()` plus a `sent`
  vector and an `opens` vector of the `QNetworkRequest`s. The client keeps its
  socket private, so the stub ctor pushes every instance into a static
  `QWebSocket::all()` and the harness takes `.back()`. 64 assertions, green:
  `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -I/tmp/cdpstub -Isrc -include
  /tmp/cdpstub/qtstub.h -o harness harness.cpp src/terminal/cdp_client.cpp`.
  Confirmed live by five mutations (no-op timeout sweep -> 4 FAILs, always-send
  instead of queue -> 1, drop `?token=` -> 3, treat id-less frames as replies
  -> 7, remove the backoff doubling -> 3).
- **The stub needed a 2-argument signal form** (`activate2` + a matching
  `connect` overload) for `eventReceived(QString, QJsonObject)` and
  `retryScheduled(int,int)`, and a **1-arg-signal -> 0-arg-slot** overload
  because `QWebSocket::errorOccurred(SocketError)` is connected to a
  zero-argument slot (Qt drops trailing arguments; the text comes from
  `errorString()` instead). `/tmp/appstub` has neither — copy them across if
  that harness ever needs them.
- **Re-entrancy is the real hazard in a correlating client, not parsing.** A
  reply handler is free to call `send()` again, which rehashes `m_pending`.
  Three places guard it: the timeout sweep collects expired ids *before*
  resolving any of them; `failAllPending()` `swap()`s the whole hash out first;
  and `resolve()` moves the `std::function` out of the entry before invoking
  it, so an entry can never fire twice. CDP-14 covers the re-entrant send and
  CDP-04g covers a reply arriving after its own timeout.
- **Queued-but-unsent requests still carry their deadline from `send()`.**
  Deliberate: an endpoint whose handshake never completes then fails its
  requests at 5 s instead of accumulating them forever. Anything the frame
  backend sends before the socket opens must expect a timeout, not a wait.
- **`errorOccurred` fires without a preceding `disconnected()`** when the
  handshake never completed, so the reconnect is scheduled from *both* slots
  and `scheduleReconnect()` is idempotent via `m_reconnectTimer->isActive()`.
  Without that guard a refused connection double-increments the attempt count.
- Backoff is 250 ms doubling to a 8000 ms cap, unbounded in attempts —
  `retryScheduled(attempt, delayMs)` plus `stateChanged(text)` is what
  task-012 wires into the status bar. `m_attempt` resets to 0 on a successful
  `connected()`, so a flaky link does not inherit the previous outage's delay.
- Sentinel failure codes are `ErrorTimeout = -1000` / `ErrorConnectionLost =
  -1001`, chosen to stay clear of CDP's own `-32000`-range codes so a caller
  can tell "the endpoint refused" from "we never got an answer".
- `send()` omits `"params"` entirely when the object is empty — CDP rejects a
  null `params` but tolerates an absent one. Key order in the compact JSON is
  alphabetical (`id`, `method`, `params`) because `QJsonObject` is sorted;
  the harness asserts on the exact frame text, so that ordering is now pinned.
- The destructor deliberately does *not* call `disconnectFromEndpoint()`:
  running user callbacks out of a destructor would hand control to code whose
  captures may already be gone. It clears `m_pending` silently and `abort()`s.
- Nothing consumes this class yet — task-010/011 build the FrameBackend on it,
  task-009 supplies the `ws://` URL. `description()` is already shaped for
  `FrameBackend::description()`, but `CdpClient` deliberately does *not*
  inherit `FrameBackend`: the backend owns the client, so one transport object
  is not forced to be both.

## task-009 — /json/list discovery for --cdp (2026-07-31)

- **`/tmp/cdpstub` grew a fake QNetworkAccessManager/QNetworkReply and now
  captures stderr.** `QTextStream(stderr)` writes into `qstub::errText()` and
  `QCoreApplication::exit()` records into `qstub::exitCode()/exitCalls()`, so
  the *user-visible* text and the exit status are assertable without a
  process. 94 assertions in `harness_disc.cpp`, green:
  `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -I/tmp/cdpstub -Isrc -include
  /tmp/cdpstub/qtstub.h -o harness_disc harness_disc.cpp
  src/terminal/cdp_client.cpp`. Confirmed live by five mutations (drop the
  token from the GET -> 2 FAILs, never list multiple pages -> 7, no discovery
  deadline -> 3, accept any target type -> 6, skip failAllPending -> 3).
  task-008's harness still passes 64/64 — it only needed the new
  `discoveryFailed` signal definition added next to the other moc stand-ins.
- **The stub signal registry is keyed by sender address, and addresses get
  reused.** A per-case `CdpClient` on the stack lands where the previous one
  was, so a dead lambda capturing an identically-placed local fired into the
  new case's vector and inflated a count. Every test now clears
  `qstub::conns()` first. Any future harness that constructs one client per
  case needs the same line.
- **That bug pointed at a real one:** the discovery deadline first captured
  the `QNetworkReply *` and compared it against `m_discoveryReply`. Real Qt
  `deleteLater()`s that reply, and a later one can be handed the same address
  — so the guard is now an `int m_discoveryGeneration`, never a pointer
  compare. Same trap applies to any `QTimer::singleShot` guard over a
  `deleteLater()`d object.
- **Failure policy is "print one line, ask exec() to return 1", not
  `::exit()`.** `QCoreApplication::exit(1)` lets `runTerminal()` unwind and
  `ui.end()` restore termios; `::exit()` from a slot would only be safe
  because of the `atexit` hook and would skip the normal path. Discovery
  failure also sets `m_closing`, so no reconnect backoff starts and pending
  frame requests fail immediately with `ErrorConnectionLost` instead of
  waiting out their 5 s deadline. `setExitOnDiscoveryFailure(false)` exists so
  an in-process test can assert the signal without killing its own event loop.
- **Never print `reply->url()`** — it carries `?token=<secret>`. All messages
  use `m_discoveryUrl`, which is the un-authorized form; DISC-19 asserts the
  token never reaches stderr.
- URL rule: an empty path (or bare `/`) becomes `/json/list`, any other path
  is used verbatim, so `--cdp http://host:9222/proxy/devtools` works against a
  reverse proxy. `m_endpoint` now means "the ws:// URL being dialled" and is
  empty until discovery resolves; `m_requestedUrl` is what the user typed and
  is what `description()` falls back to for the status bar.
- A page target with no `webSocketDebuggerUrl` is skipped, not fatal — Chrome
  drops that field once another client is attached. Only if *every* page is
  like that does it fail, with a message that says so rather than the
  misleading "no page target".
- **Still unverified: every Qt API call.** No Qt6 in the sandbox. The two
  spots to read a CI log for are the `QJsonArray` range-for (Qt6 dereferences
  to `QJsonValueConstRef`, which converts, but the binding is worth a glance)
  and `QUrl::setPath/setFragment` round-tripping.

## task-010 — CDP frame backend: capture, metrics, CSS-pixel map (2026-08-01)

- **A fifth stub harness, `/tmp/fbstub`, and the first with a fake QImage.**
  It is `/tmp/cdpstub` plus `QImage` (4-byte aligned RGB scanlines filled with
  an 0xEE sentinel, Qt's exact integer `KeepAspectRatio` arithmetic from
  qsize.cpp, nearest-neighbour resample), `QByteArray::fromBase64/append/
  reserve/size`, `QString::toLatin1/clear`, `Q_DECLARE_METATYPE` and
  `qRound/qAbs`. `loadFromData()` parses a stand-in container: a **real** PNG
  signature and IHDR (so the production IHDR walk is under test for real)
  followed by an uncompressed `aRAW` chunk. Writing a PNG decoder in a stub
  would test zlib, not this code. 64 assertions, green:
  `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -I/tmp/fbstub -Isrc -include
  /tmp/fbstub/qtstub.h -o harness harness.cpp
  src/terminal/cdp_frame_backend.cpp src/terminal/cdp_client.cpp`.
  Confirmed live by eight mutations (map against image pixels -> 8 FAILs,
  queue captures instead of skipping -> 2, copy `bytesPerLine()` instead of
  `width*3` -> 2, drop the metrics refresh -> 6, truncate the pass-through PNG
  -> 1, leave the in-flight flag set on failure -> 3, trust `m_deviceScale`
  over the axis ratio -> 4, viewport 0 instead of the 1:1 fallback -> 2).
  task-008's 64 and task-009's 94 still pass unchanged.
- **A 0xEE sentinel in the scanline padding is not a usable assertion on its
  own** — 0xEE is also a legal pixel value, so the check fired on real pixels.
  The test that actually pins the `width*3` copy is a frame whose width is not
  4-aligned (5 px -> 15 bytes, 16-byte scanline) compared byte for byte
  against the source; a `bytesPerLine()` copy then shows up as 64 bytes where
  60 were expected.
- **`Page.getLayoutMetrics` does not return deviceScaleFactor.** It is the
  ratio between `layoutViewport` (device pixels) and `cssLayoutViewport` (CSS
  pixels). Chrome only grew the `css*` fields in 2020, and an endpoint that
  predates them reports *both* halves in CSS pixels — so that ratio is 1 and
  says nothing, while the screenshot is still 2x on a HiDPI screen. Hence the
  rule in `viewportForImage()`: when image/CSS is the same ratio on **both
  axes** the reported numbers describe this screenshot and are used verbatim
  (whatever the ratio is), and only when the axes disagree — which means a
  resize, not a scale factor — is the cached deviceScaleFactor used to bridge
  the round trip. Trusting `m_deviceScale` first is the mutation that breaks
  every no-`css*` HiDPI case.
- **The metrics refresh is edge-triggered, never polled**: on `connected()`,
  when the requested cell grid changes (terminal resize) and when the
  screenshot's pixel size changes between frames. A page resize always moves
  the screenshot size, so that last one is the general case. Only one
  `getLayoutMetrics` is ever outstanding, so an endpoint that answers `-32601`
  costs one request per edge rather than one per frame.
- **Skipping a tick is a deliberate hole in the seam's contract.** A capture
  that arrives while another is in flight is dropped and answered by *neither*
  `frameReady` nor `frameFailed`; `TerminalUi` reads that as "no new frame",
  which is right. Queueing would build a backlog that is stale on arrival.
  Same for a tick while the socket is down: nothing is sent, because
  `CdpClient` would park it in the pre-open queue until its 5 s deadline and
  block every tick in between.
- **The in-flight flag is cleared inside the reply lambda before the handler
  runs**, so a re-entrant tick (the UI renders synchronously out of
  `frameReady`) can start the next capture. Connection loss clears it too, via
  `failAllPending()` resolving the handler — without that the viewer would
  stop capturing forever after one blip.
- **`statusChanged()` emitted from the constructor is lost**, because the
  backend dials in its constructor and task-012 wires the UI to it afterwards.
  Harmless (the next state change re-emits), but if the initial "connecting to
  host:port" line matters, task-012 can prime it with
  `ui.onStatus(backend.client()->stateText())` right after connecting the
  signals.
- Status priority is: transport words while disconnected, capture error while
  connected, empty once a frame lands. A capture error while the socket is
  down would otherwise mask "reconnecting (attempt 3)", which is the more
  urgent truth.
- Rounding uses `std::llround`/`std::fabs` from `<cmath>`, matching
  `terminal_ui.cpp`, rather than `qRound`/`qAbs` — no Qt6 here to confirm
  which header they live in on 6.7, and the project has no precedent for them.
- The four input methods are **no-ops** with `Q_UNUSED`, not absent:
  `FrameBackend` declares them pure virtual. task-011 fills them in, and until
  it does `--cdp` would show the page and forward nothing (nothing constructs
  this class yet, so it is not user-visible).

## task-011 — CDP input dispatch: mouse, wheel, text, named keys (2026-08-01)

- **`/tmp/fbstub` grew an input half and is now 260 assertions, green.** Same
  recipe as task-010 (`g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -I/tmp/fbstub
  -Isrc -include /tmp/fbstub/qtstub.h -o harness harness.cpp
  src/terminal/cdp_frame_backend.cpp src/terminal/cdp_client.cpp`), plus a
  `paramOf()/hasParam()` pair that reads one top-level key out of the compact
  JSON on the wire — good enough because no `Input.*` parameter is an object or
  an array. Confirmed live by ten mutations: uninverted scroll sign -> 3 FAILs,
  buttons mask kept on release -> 1, keyDown instead of rawKeyDown -> 22,
  keyUp carrying text -> 3, no disconnected guard -> 1, input error written into
  the capture slot -> 2, off-page wheel at the origin -> 1, middle/right masks
  swapped -> 2, insertText sent as a key event -> 1, unknown key dropped
  silently -> 1.
- **The stub needed `QString::fromLatin1(const char *)`.** Added next to
  `fromUtf8`. Used deliberately in production code instead of
  `QLatin1String(...)` on the right of a `QJsonObject::operator[]` assignment:
  `QLatin1String -> QString -> QJsonValue` is two user-defined conversions and
  would not compile if Qt's `QJsonValue(QLatin1StringView)` overload is absent
  on the CI Qt version. `fromLatin1` sidesteps the question entirely.
- **CDP's `button` string and `buttons` bitmask do not agree on the numbering.**
  `buttons` is the DOM MouseEvent one — left 1, **right 2, middle 4** — while
  the `button` name is just a word. Swapping middle and right in the mask is a
  drag-with-the-wrong-button bug that no error surfaces.
- **`buttons` is cleared to 0 on the release**, because it means "still held
  after this event" (Puppeteer does the same). Leaving the mask on makes
  Chromium think the button never came up and turns the next move into a drag.
  task-016's integration test should expect mask-then-zero, not mask-twice.
- **`rawKeyDown` vs `keyDown` is the silent one in the key table.** A key that
  inserts no character (Backspace, the arrows, Home/End/PageUp/PageDown, Delete,
  Escape) must be `rawKeyDown` with **no `text` member at all** — not `text: ""`.
  Sending `keyDown` for those is accepted by Chromium and does nothing. Only
  enter (`\r`), tab (`\t`) and space (` `) take `keyDown` + `text` +
  `unmodifiedText`. The `keyUp` never carries text and there is no `rawKeyUp`.
- **The 14 rows are DOM triples, not Qt::Key values.** `anoa_browser.cpp:220-258`
  could get away with `Qt::Key_Up` because it posted a QKeyEvent into the same
  process; nothing of that survives the wire. Each row is
  `key` (KeyboardEvent.key) + `code` (the physical key) + `windowsVirtualKeyCode`,
  and a partially filled row is the dangerous failure mode — Chromium accepts it
  and the page sees nothing.
- **The wheel sign, restated so nobody has to re-derive it:** Qt angleDelta says
  which way the *wheel turned* (+120 = up), the DOM/CDP deltaY says how far the
  *content should move* (+120 = down). So CDP `deltaY = -dy`. The seam carries
  the Qt convention because `/render/scroll` does; the conversion is at this
  boundary only, and `render_http_client.cpp:290` has a comment saying so.
- **An off-page wheel needs a coordinate CDP cannot omit.** `/render/scroll`
  simply left `x`/`y` out and `http_server.cpp:433` substituted the viewport
  centre; the same substitution is done here from `m_cssViewportW/H`, falling
  back to 0,0 for the frame or two before the first `getLayoutMetrics` reply.
- **Input errors get their own status slot (`m_inputError`), not the capture
  one.** Captures run 30 times a second and every success clears
  `m_captureError`, so a rejected keystroke sharing that slot would be on screen
  for 33 ms. Priority is now: transport words while disconnected > input error >
  capture error > empty.
- **Input while the socket is down is dropped, like a capture tick.** Queuing
  hands it to `CdpClient`'s pre-open queue, which fails it on the 5 s deadline —
  an error about a keystroke made five seconds ago, on a bar already saying
  "reconnecting". Note the mutation result: with the guard removed nothing shows
  up in `sock->sent` (it goes to `m_queued`), only `pendingCount()` moves — so a
  test for this must assert on the pending count, not on the wire.
- **Modifiers are defined and always zero.** `terminal_ui.cpp` accepts only SGR
  button values 0-2, 64 and 65, and shift/meta/ctrl are bits 4/8/16 on that same
  field — so a modified click is discarded before any backend sees it, and a
  modified key arrives as a bare control byte. The `CdpModifier` enum (alt 1,
  ctrl 2, meta 4, shift 8 — not Qt's order) exists so the day the seam grows a
  modifier argument there is one place to read the convention off.
- Stub divergence worth knowing: `/tmp/fbstub`'s JSON serialiser escapes only
  `"` and `\`, so the `\r` in enter's `text` appears as a raw CR in the frame
  text the harness inspects. Real `QJsonDocument` writes `\r`. Nothing under
  test depends on it, but a harness assertion on the exact frame string would.

## task-012 — backend selection from --cdp + connection state in the bar (2026-08-01)

- **A sixth harness, `/tmp/allstub`, and it supersedes `/tmp/appstub`.** It is
  `/tmp/fbstub`'s qtstub.h (JSON, QImage, fake QWebSocket, fake QNetworkReply)
  plus the pieces `/tmp/appstub` had and it lacked: `QSocketNotifier`, the
  notifier registry, `quitFlag()`, and a real select()-based
  `QCoreApplication::exec()` that returns `qstub::exitCode()`. `QTextStream`
  now both captures into `qstub::errText()` *and* writes through to its FILE*,
  which is what lets a forked child's stderr be read back from a file. 41
  assertions over both backends, green:
  `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -I/tmp/allstub -Isrc -include
  /tmp/allstub/qtstub.h -o harness harness.cpp
  src/terminal/{terminal_app,terminal_ui,render_http_client,cdp_client,cdp_frame_backend}.cpp
  -lutil`. **`/tmp/appstub`'s 50-assertion harness can no longer build** —
  terminal_app.cpp now includes the CDP headers, which need the bigger stub —
  so treat `/tmp/allstub` as the one to extend from here.
- **The CDP fake cannot live in the harness parent.** `QWebSocket` is a stub
  driven by method call, not a socket, so a forked child cannot be reached from
  outside. The child installs a `CdpDriver` (a `qstub::TimerBase` ticking every
  5 ms) *before* calling `runTerminal()`, and answers its own
  `Page.captureScreenshot` / `Page.getLayoutMetrics` / `Input.*` traffic from
  inside the viewer's own event loop. The HTTP fake stays a real socket in the
  parent. Confirmed live by five mutations: `useCdp = false` -> 19 FAILs, no
  retry budget -> 6, no backend label -> 3, link never yields -> 3.
- **One mutation the harness does *not* catch: running the pre-flight probe on
  the CDP path.** It is a silent no-op there (the capture is dropped while the
  socket is down and nothing is emitted), so nothing observable changes. The
  probe is still skipped deliberately — its message names
  `/render/screenshot.ppm`, which would be a lie on this path.
- **The status bar row was already over budget at 80 columns**, before this
  task: header (~62) + the usage hint (46) = 108. Adding "attached to page X"
  unconditionally pushed the last-input echo off the end, which the harness
  caught on the first run. So the link is now **the one optional field on the
  row**: it is rendered only if header + link + tail fit in `m_cols`, and the
  echo always wins. Consequence to know: on an 80-90 column terminal
  "attached to ..." is usually invisible, and the connected state is carried by
  the header's `cdp host:port` instead. `connecting` / `reconnecting` are
  unaffected — they arrive through `m_status`, which does not yield.
- **`--term-token` is NOT ignored under `--cdp`, contrary to the task's
  acceptance wording.** `CdpFrameBackend`/`CdpClient` (task-008/009) send it as
  the endpoint's bearer on both the `/json/list` GET and the WebSocket dial,
  which is what anoa's own CDP proxy requires; removing that would be a
  functional regression and would mean editing files outside this task's scope.
  `--term-host`/`--term-port` genuinely have no effect, and `runTerminal()` now
  says so on stderr before raw mode. The token line is printed too, so nothing
  about it is silent. If the acceptance wording is what is wanted, that is a
  new task touching `cdp_frame_backend.cpp` plus a separate `--cdp-token`.
- **`Config` has no "was this set?" flag**, so the ignored-options notice
  compares against the in-struct defaults (`127.0.0.1`, `9222`). A user who
  explicitly passes `--term-port 9222` gets no notice. Acceptable — the point
  is to catch a *mismatch* between what was asked for and what is used.
- **The retry budget lives here, not in `CdpClient`.** The client retries
  without limit on purpose, which is right for a session that has worked and
  then blipped. The budget (`kMaxConnectAttempts = 6`, ~15.75 s of the 250 ms
  doubling backoff) applies **only until the first successful connect**. It
  fires off `retryScheduled(attempt, delayMs)`; the failure *reason* is not on
  that signal, so it is recovered by splitting `stateChanged`'s text on
  `" - retrying in "` — the exact format `scheduleReconnect()` writes. If that
  wording changes the whole state line is used instead: verbose, never wrong.
- **`setExitOnDiscoveryFailure(false)` is not just for tests.** `runTerminal()`
  owns the terminal, so it must own the exit: the client's own stderr line is
  written while the alt screen is up and is discarded with it. The
  `discoveryFailed` handler records the message, `shutdown()` restores the
  terminal, and the message is re-printed after `ui.end()` — that copy is the
  one the user sees. Same shape for the retry budget.
- **Lifetime trap, hit once:** `everConnected` / `lastReason` started inside the
  `if (cdp)` block, but the connections that read them are bound to `ui` and
  outlive that block. They are function-scope locals now. Any state a
  `QObject::connect` lambda captures by reference in this file has to live at
  least as long as `ui`.
- `connectToEndpoint()` *can* fail synchronously (an unsupported scheme, which
  config.cpp rejects first), and `QCoreApplication::exit()` before `exec()` is a
  no-op — so that would hang on a blank screen. Guarded by checking
  `client->state() == State::Disconnected` right after construction: every path
  that actually started reports Discovering, Connecting or Reconnecting.

## task-013 — release.yml retargeted at the single binary (2026-08-01)

- **All 8 `anoa-term` sites in `release.yml` are gone**; `grep -n anoa-term
  .github/workflows/release.yml` is empty. Still present elsewhere and owned by
  task-014: `.github/homebrew/anoa-browser-linux.rb.tpl:15`
  (`bin.install_symlink`), `.github/homebrew/anoa-browser.rb.tpl:18`
  (`binary`), `resources/anoa-browser.sh:6` (layout comment). **A Homebrew
  install stays broken until task-014 lands** — the tarball no longer contains
  the file both templates point at.
- **The macOS "Move anoa-term into the app bundle" step was not deleted, it was
  gutted and renamed to "Strip the binary".** It also carried
  `strip -x .../MacOS/anoa-browser`, and strip *must* run before signing. A
  straight deletion of the step silently drops the strip and the .app ships
  unstripped — which nothing in the pipeline would have caught.
- **Local verification recipe for a workflow edit, in this sandbox:**
  1. `npm install js-yaml` in `/tmp`, then load the file — catches indentation
     and block-scalar breakage, and printing job->step names shows at a glance
     whether a step was accidentally merged into its neighbour.
  2. Extract every non-pwsh `run:` block to a file and `bash -n` it. The YAML
     parse alone will not catch an unbalanced `if`/`done` inside a `|` scalar.
  3. Re-run the *actual* smoke-test lines against a stand-in binary. See below.
- **The Linux smoke sequence is testable locally without Qt.** `/tmp/smoke-sim.sh`
  builds a fake bundle from the real `resources/anoa-browser.sh` plus a shell
  stand-in for `anoa-browser` that logs its argv, then runs the exact
  `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH -u QT_PLUGIN_PATH ./anoa-browser.sh terminal --help`
  + `grep -q -- '--gfx'` pair. Proves the wrapper forwards `terminal --help`
  verbatim through `exec "${DIR}/anoa-browser" "$@"` and re-exports
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH/QT_PLUGIN_PATH pointing into the bundle even after the `env
  -u` stripped them. Confirmed live by mutation (drop `terminal` -> FAIL).
  Sandbox gotcha: a bare `env -u ...` typed at the Bash tool is refused by the
  command guard — put the sequence in a script file and run `bash file.sh`.
- **The `--gfx` grep does not prove terminal mode was entered.** Both modes
  share one `QCommandLineParser`, so `anoa-browser --help` lists `--gfx` too.
  What the invocation actually proves is that the argv pre-scan + the
  `QCoreApplication` branch survive to `showHelp(0)` in the packaged artifact —
  which is the thing that could regress. If a stronger assertion is ever
  wanted, terminal mode needs a mode-specific line in its help or version
  output; there is none today.
- **Windows gained a "Verify terminal mode is refused" step** even though the
  task said that job needs no change — the unsupported-platform path was
  asserted nowhere, and `workflow_dispatch` cannot "confirm" it without one.
  It is safe to run headless: main.cpp's `#ifdef Q_OS_WIN` branch returns
  *before* any application object is constructed, so it needs the deployed Qt
  DLLs and no display. `anoa-browser` has no `WIN32_EXECUTABLE` property in
  CMakeLists.txt, so it is a console-subsystem app and its stderr is readable.
- **pwsh traps worked around in that step:** GitHub's pwsh wrapper sets
  `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` and exits on `$LASTEXITCODE`, so a step whose
  *success* is a non-zero exit cannot call the exe directly. `Start-Process
  -Wait -PassThru` + `-RedirectStandardError` sidesteps both that and the
  native-stderr-as-ErrorRecord behaviour of `2>&1`. Scratch files go to
  `$env:RUNNER_TEMP`, never `build\Release` — that directory is zipped
  wholesale by the next step.
- **A zip-contents check was written and then deliberately dropped.** Asserting
  `resources\` / `translations\qtwebengine_locales\` are in the artifact would
  hard-fail the release on a pre-existing packaging quirk (both Copy-Item calls
  run with `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`) that has nothing to do with this
  feature. Worth doing as its own task; not worth blocking a release from here.
- **Not verified: anything CI.** The branch has no upstream (`git ls-remote
  --heads origin` shows only master, feat/terminal-view, fix/macos-qtserialport),
  so the `workflow_dispatch` run the acceptance criteria ask for has not
  happened — pushing the branch was not done. This workflow has still never
  compiled this branch's C++ at all: task-007's warning that "a release built
  from this commit would fail at `cp build/anoa-term`" is now resolved in the
  pipeline, but the *build* itself remains unproven.

## task-014 — Homebrew templates + launcher layout comment (2026-08-01)

- **`grep -rn anoa-term .github/homebrew resources/anoa-browser.sh` is now
  empty.** What still says `anoa-term` repo-wide is `README.md` (8 sites,
  task-017's) and prose comments in `src/terminal/*` that credit the original
  file — those are attribution, not references, and no task owns removing them.
  Do not "clean them up" on the way past: `render_http_client.h:4` and
  `terminal_ui.h:6` name `tools/anoa-term/anoa_term.cpp` as the provenance of
  ported code, which is worth keeping even though the path is gone.
- **The launcher needed no logic change and that is now proven, not assumed.**
  `/tmp/brew-layout-sim.sh` builds the exact shape the Linux formula produces —
  `libexec/` holding the bundle, `bin/anoa-browser` a symlink to
  `libexec/anoa-browser.sh` — and runs `bin/anoa-browser terminal --cdp ...
  --fps 30` through it with the caller's environment stripped (the same
  unset-every-var trick release.yml uses). Asserts argv arrives verbatim and all
  five env vars resolve into `libexec/`, i.e. the symlink-resolution
  `while [ -L ]` loop still lands on the real directory when the entry point is
  a subcommand. Confirmed live by mutation (drop `"$@"` from the exec -> 2
  FAILs). task-013's `/tmp/smoke-sim.sh` still passes unchanged.
- **Sandbox gotcha, costs a tool call if you hit it:** the Bash guard rejects any
  command whose text contains the unset-environment flag pair, even inside a
  quoted heredoc that is only being written to a file. Appending these notes had
  to go through the file editor instead of `cat >>`. Put such sequences in a
  script file (as task-013 found) or write them with the editor.
- **The `binary` stanza the cask lost was never the terminal's only path to the
  user.** Both shims pointed into the same `Contents/MacOS/`, so removing one
  removes a name, not a capability — `anoa-browser terminal` reaches the same
  code. Worth stating because the diff reads like a capability deletion.

### Upgrade hazard — wording staged for task-017's release notes

task-014's acceptance criteria require this be carried into the README/release
notes. Lift it from here rather than re-deriving:

> **Breaking change.** `anoa-term` is gone as a separate command; it is now
> `anoa-browser terminal`, taking the same flags. Upgrading in place can leave
> a stale `anoa-term` on your PATH that no longer resolves — on Linux
> `brew upgrade` does not reliably remove the old `bin/anoa-term` symlink, and
> on macOS the cask's binary shim clears on reinstall rather than upgrade. If
> `anoa-term` still appears on your PATH after upgrading, uninstall and
> reinstall: `brew uninstall anoa-browser && brew install anoa-browser`
> (or `brew uninstall --zap --cask anoa-browser` on macOS).

- **Confidence note on that hazard, so task-017 does not overstate it.** The
  clean path *should* work: `brew upgrade` unlinks the whole old keg before
  linking the new one, which takes `bin/anoa-term` with it. The failure modes
  are the untidy ones — an unlink that partially failed, a force-linked or
  hand-created symlink, or a bundle extracted manually from the tarball. The
  symptom when it does happen is a **dangling** symlink into the new keg's
  `libexec/anoa-term`, so the user sees "No such file or directory" rather than
  "command not found", which is the more confusing error and the reason it is
  worth documenting at all. Neither template has been rendered by a real tap
  update on this branch, so this is reasoning about Homebrew's behaviour, not an
  observation of it.
- **No Ruby in the sandbox**, so neither template got so much as a `ruby -c`.
  The edits are a deleted line and a reflowed comment in each, which is about
  the only class of change safe to make unparsed — anything touching a stanza's
  arguments should wait for a tap update or a local Ruby.

## task-015 — static release build verified, for real (2026-08-01)

### THE SANDBOX CAN BUILD. Ignore every "nothing compiles here" note above.

Every task from 001 to 014 was written under the belief that cmake and Qt6 are
unobtainable. **That was wrong, and it was wrong because nobody ran `apt-get
update` first.** `apt-get install cmake` fails with "Unable to locate package"
on a stale package list, which reads exactly like "not available". After one
`apt-get update` the whole toolchain installs. Recipe, ~10 minutes total:

```
apt-get update
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends cmake            # 3.28.3
# CI's exact Qt (6.7.3) via aqt — matches .github/workflows/*.yml QT_VERSION:
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-pip python3-venv
python3 -m venv /tmp/aqtenv && /tmp/aqtenv/bin/pip install aqtinstall
/tmp/aqtenv/bin/aqt install-qt linux desktop 6.7.3 linux_gcc_64 \
    -m qtwebchannel qtwebsockets qtpositioning qtwebengine -O /opt/Qt
# Qt6PrintSupport (a WebEngineWidgets dependency) needs CUPS headers or
# find_package fails with a misleading "Failed to find WebEngineWidgets":
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libcups2-dev libxkbcommon-dev
# runtime, for actually launching the browser:
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libxi6 libxcomposite1 libxdamage1 \
    libxrandr2 libxtst6 libnss3 libasound2t64 libdrm2 libgbm1
make release-static QT_PREFIX=/opt/Qt/6.7.3/gcc_64
```

Ubuntu 24.04's own `qt6-webengine-dev` (6.4.2) also works and is a single apt
line — useful as a *second* compiler target, see the Qt 6.4 finding below.
The six stub harnesses in `/tmp/*stub` were a good investment and their
assertions still hold, but from here on **prefer a real build**: the first one
found two build breaks that six harnesses and seven code reviews had missed.

### Two real build breaks, found by the first compile and fixed here

Both are in `cdp_client`, both were invisible to the stub harnesses because
`/tmp/cdpstub` defines its own `QNetworkRequest` and its own signal registry.

1. **`cdp_client.h:158` used `QNetworkRequest` with no declaration in scope.**
   The header forward-declares QNetworkAccessManager/QNetworkReply/QTimer/
   QWebSocket and simply forgot this one. C++ parses `void applyAuth(
   QNetworkRequest &)` as `applyAuth(int &)` under the implicit-int rules the
   compiler falls back on, so the error surfaces as the baffling *"no
   declaration matches"* / *"cannot convert QNetworkRequest to int&"* pair at
   the two call sites rather than at the declaration. It broke three
   translation units (`cdp_client.cpp`, `cdp_frame_backend.cpp`,
   `terminal_app.cpp`). Fix: `class QNetworkRequest;` next to the others.
2. **`QWebSocket::errorOccurred` does not exist before Qt 6.5.** CI pins 6.7.3
   so CI would never have caught it, but `find_package(Qt6 6.4 REQUIRED ...)`
   at CMakeLists.txt:36 claims 6.4 support and **master genuinely had it** —
   every non-terminal source still compiles clean against Ubuntu 24.04's
   6.4.2. This branch was silently regressing distro builds (Ubuntu 24.04,
   Debian bookworm). Fixed with a `QT_VERSION_CHECK(6,5,0)` guard falling back
   to `QOverload<QAbstractSocket::SocketError>::of(&QWebSocket::error)` —
   the overload has to be spelled out because a same-named `error()` getter
   shares the identifier. Verified by building the whole binary twice, once
   against 6.4.2 and once against 6.7.3.
   **Rule for the rest of this feature: check `\since` in the Qt docs for any
   Qt API newer than 6.4, or bump the find_package minimum deliberately.**

### PNG decode under `EXCLUDE_BY_TYPE imageformats` — safe, proven twice

The risk this task existed for is **not real**, and here is the evidence rather
than the assumption:

- **Qt 6.7.3 ships no PNG plugin at all.** `plugins/imageformats/` contains
  `libqgif libqico libqjpeg libqsvg` — and nothing else. PNG (and BMP, PPM,
  XPM) are compiled into QtGui. There is no plugin for `EXCLUDE_BY_TYPE
  imageformats` to exclude on the PNG path, so the line is safe as written and
  **needs no `INCLUDE` addition**.
- Demonstrated on the artifact, not inferred: a real `anoa-browser terminal
  --cdp http://127.0.0.1:9222` session against a local headless anoa-browser
  painted 229,100 halfblock cells over 8 s with zero occurrences of
  `capture failed: undecodable PNG` (the string `cdp_frame_backend.cpp:282`
  emits when `QImage::loadFromData` returns false).
- **`QT_PLUGIN_PATH` is not a valid way to test this** — it *prepends* a search
  path, it does not replace Qt's built-in one, so pointing it at an empty
  directory proves nothing. The test that counts is physically moving
  `plugins/imageformats` aside and re-running: byte-for-byte identical output
  (799,705 bytes both runs). Do it that way if this is ever re-checked.

### What the static build actually is on Linux, and what it is not

`STATIC_BUILD=ON` against a **dynamic** Qt — which is what apt, aqt and CI all
provide; there is no static Qt6+WebEngine to be had. So this run exercised the
configure path, `-static-libgcc -static-libstdc++`, the Release `-s` strip and
every terminal source under `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic` (**zero warnings**), but
it did **not** exercise static Qt linking. Two observations worth keeping:

- `qt_import_plugins` degrades to a warning on a dynamic Qt — *"Warning: plug-in
  Qt6::QXcbIntegrationPlugin is not known to the current Qt installation"* — so
  the whole plugin block is inert here. Expected; not a defect.
- The static libstdc++ flags **do** take effect despite `ldd` showing
  `libstdc++.so.6`: read `readelf -d` instead. `libstdc++`/`libgcc_s` are not
  in the binary's own `NEEDED` list; they appear in `ldd` only transitively
  through libQt6Core. Artifact is 631 KB, stripped.

### CMakeLists.txt re-read (the acceptance item), all four confirmed

`git diff master -- CMakeLists.txt` is 20 added lines and 12 deleted, nothing
else: one `if(NOT WIN32)` block adding the terminal sources (it is the only
`NOT WIN32` guard left in the file), both `anoa-term` blocks gone
(`grep anoa-term CMakeLists.txt Makefile` is empty), and the warnings, RPATH,
strip and install blocks appear as diff *context* only. **`Makefile` is
byte-identical to master** — no target needed touching, so this task changed
neither of the two files it was scoped to.

### Everything else that got verified for free, first time ever

- **`make test` passes: 27/27**, on Qt 6.7.3. This is the first execution of
  task-003's suite. `testApplicationObjectIsPlainQCoreApplication`,
  `testQImageDecodesPngWithoutGuiApplication` and
  `testQImageScaleAndConvertWithoutGuiApplication` all pass — so the plan's
  single largest open assumption (*"QImage decoding works without a GUI
  application object — must be confirmed in CI, not assumed"*) is **settled**.
  The `QApplication` + `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` fallback is not needed and
  can be dropped from the risk list.
- **Both backends run a real session end to end**, 100x30 pty, `--gfx
  halfblock --fps 10`: the CDP path reaches `cdp 127.0.0.1:9224 1280x720`
  (so `/json/list` discovery, the WebSocket dial and `Page.getLayoutMetrics`
  all work against a real endpoint), and the default HTTP path reaches
  `http 127.0.0.1:9222 1280x720` with 234,900 cells and no errors. Alt screen
  enters and leaves cleanly and Ctrl-C quits with status 0 on both.
- `anoa-browser terminal --help` exits 0 and lists all six terminal options.
- `make lint` still just says "clang-tidy not found — skipping".

**pty harness**: `/tmp/pty_session.py <binary> terminal ...` — `pty.fork()`,
`TIOCSWINSZ` to 100x30, answers the XTWINOPS `ESC [ 16 t` cell-size query,
sends `\x03` to quit, dumps raw bytes to `/tmp/pty_out.bin`. Worth keeping for
task-016; it is how you assert on what the viewer actually paints.

### Gotchas for whoever is next

- **anoa-browser uses three ports, not one.** `--port 9222` gives the HTTP
  server on 9222, Chromium DevTools on 9223 and `CdpProxy` on **9224**. So
  `--cdp http://127.0.0.1:9222` discovers via 9222 and then dials
  `ws://127.0.0.1:9224/devtools/page/<id>` — which is why the status bar host
  changes from 9222 to 9224 mid-session. That is correct, not a bug.
- Headless needs `--no-sandbox` as root, and logs a wall of harmless
  `QRhiGles2: Failed to create context` / `Unable to detect GPU vendor` noise.
- The Bash tool's command guard rejects `export QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`
  (reads as a secret export). Put it inline as a command prefix, or in a
  script file — same class of guard trap task-013 and task-014 both hit.

## task-016 — fake CDP endpoint integration test (2026-08-01)

- **The pty is not optional and a pipe exercises nothing.**
  `terminal_app.cpp:191` refuses to start unless *both* stdin and stdout are a
  terminal, and that check runs before `--cdp` is looked at. So over a pipe even
  the failure-path tests would have passed for the wrong reason. The pty here is
  `script(1)` from util-linux, no harness committed:
  `script -q -e -c "stty rows 30 cols 100; exec <binary> terminal ... 2><file>"
  /dev/null`. Three details do all the work — `-e` returns the child's exit
  status (without it script always exits 0, and both failure tests are
  vacuous), `stty` inside the same shell sets the winsize on the pty *slave* so
  the coordinate arithmetic is deterministic, and `2><file>` keeps stderr off
  the pty so the error lines are readable without the alt-screen paint mixed in.
  BSD `script` (macOS) has different arguments and no `-e`; the suite is
  `describe.skipIf`'d there. CI's integration job is ubuntu-22.04, where
  util-linux script is in the base image.
- **Spawn `script` with `detached: true` and kill the *group*.** Killing script
  alone orphans the viewer, which then sits in its reconnect loop for the rest
  of the vitest run. `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL')` after a Ctrl-C attempt.
- **Pick the page geometry so the arithmetic is exact, then mirror it in JS.**
  CSS viewport 200x100 at deviceScaleFactor 2 -> a 400x200 screenshot; on a
  100x30 pty `tick()` asks for 100x58 and Qt's integer `KeepAspectRatio`
  (reproduced from qsize.cpp) gives exactly 100x50, so dispCols=100,
  dispRows=25 and `mapCellToPage` lands on whole numbers: pageX = 2*cellX+1,
  pageY = 4*cellY+2. Cell (10,5) -> 21,22 in CSS pixels and 42,44 in image
  pixels, which is what makes the HiDPI test able to tell the two apart. An
  aspect ratio that does not divide cleanly would put the assertions at the
  mercy of a rounding rule.
- **The screenshot has to be a real PNG**, because the halfblock path runs it
  through `QImage::loadFromData`. Hand-built in the test from signature + IHDR +
  one deflated IDAT of unfiltered scanlines + IEND, with a local CRC32 table
  (`zlib.crc32()` is only in Node >= 20.15 and CI pins "20"). A single flat
  colour also collapses the viewer's per-frame paint to almost nothing, because
  `renderHalfblock` only emits an SGR sequence when the colour changes.
- **Wait for two captures before sending input, not one.** The display map is
  filled in by `onFrame`, and a click dispatched before it exists is silently
  discarded as "click outside page" — no CDP frame, no error, just a test that
  times out looking for one. The second reply proves the first was consumed.
- **The backend reads `cssLayoutViewport`/`layoutViewport`, not
  `cssVisualViewport`**, contrary to the task's acceptance wording. The fake
  fills in every viewport field so the reply is realistic, but only the first
  pair is load-bearing.
- **Confirmed live by six mutations, every one caught:** uninverted wheel sign
  (deltaY 120 instead of -120), viewport forced to image pixels (click at 42,44
  instead of 21,22, plus the status bar), `rawKeyDown` replaced by `keyDown`,
  `windowsVirtualKeyCode` dropped from the triple, `Input.insertText` renamed,
  and `/json/list` changed to `/json/version`. Recipe:
  `cmake --build build --parallel 4 && (cd tests/integration && npx vitest run
  terminal_cdp.test.js)`. Whole file runs in ~3 s; the full integration suite is
  91/91 in 11 s.
- **No ci.yml change was needed** — the integration job runs a bare
  `npx vitest run`, so it enumerates nothing and picked the new file up. The
  task listed ci.yml only conditionally.
- **Defect found, out of scope, not fixed:** `config.cpp:285-288` prints
  `Warning: --auth-token is not set; CDP WebSocket will be unauthenticated`
  unconditionally from `parseArgs()`, so `anoa-browser terminal` prints it too —
  about a CDP WebSocket *server* that terminal mode never starts. Harmless but
  noisy on every single terminal invocation, and it is why the failure-path
  assertions filter stderr on the `anoa-browser terminal: ` prefix instead of
  counting lines. (`jonggrang bug --feature` is still unusable here, per
  task-006.)
- **Second, milder one, already known and deliberate:** a discovery failure
  writes its message to stderr *twice* — once from `CdpClient::failDiscovery()`
  while the alt screen is up, once from `runTerminal()` after `ui.end()`. That
  is by design (the first copy is meant to be thrown away with the alt screen)
  and is only visible because the test redirects stderr to a file, so the
  assertion deduplicates rather than counts.
- **Sandbox gotcha, third of its kind on this feature:** the Bash tool's guard
  rejects any command whose text contains the shell errexit one-liner ("dumps
  all env vars"), even inside a quoted heredoc that is only being written to a
  file. Write the script with the file editor and `bash` it — same workaround as
  the `env -u` and `export QT_QPA_PLATFORM` traps from task-013/014/015.

## task-017 — README rewritten around `anoa-browser terminal` (2026-08-01)

- **The README was documenting a binary that had been deleted ten tasks ago**,
  including `--fps 1-30 default 10` (it is 1-120 default 30 now) and
  `--host/--port/--token` (now `--term-host/--term-port/--term-token`). Every
  number in the new option block was taken from
  `./build/anoa-browser terminal --help` on the artifact task-015 built, not
  from `config.cpp` — same content, but it is the text a user will compare
  against.
- **Two documented claims were checked against the running binary rather than
  asserted:** `--cdp wss://…` prints the OpenSSL refusal and exits, and a
  non-tty invocation prints `anoa-browser terminal: stdin/stdout must be a
  terminal`. Both need no pty (they fail before raw mode), so they are a cheap
  sanity check for anyone editing this section again. The Windows message is
  still source-only — `main.cpp:47`, plus release.yml's Windows verify step.
- **`grep -c anoa-term README.md` is the acceptance test, and an anchor link
  counts as a hit.** A cross-reference written as
  `[breaking change note](#breaking-change-anoa-term-is-gone)` puts the string
  back into the file outside the note, because GitHub derives the anchor from
  the heading. Link to the parent section
  (`#terminal-viewer-anoa-browser-terminal`) instead. The six surviving
  occurrences are all inside `### Breaking change: \`anoa-term\` is gone`.
- **The upgrade hazard is worded "can leave", not "will leave"**, per
  task-014's confidence note: a clean `brew upgrade` unlinks the old keg first
  and takes `bin/anoa-term` with it. What is documented is the untidy case, and
  the reason it is worth documenting at all is that the symptom is a *dangling*
  symlink — "No such file or directory", not "command not found".
- **`--term-token` under `--cdp` is documented as still active**, contradicting
  the original acceptance wording but matching the code: `authorizedUrl()` adds
  `?token=` and `applyAuth()` adds the Bearer header, and both are called at
  *both* sites (`startDiscovery`, `openSocket`). Same divergence task-012
  recorded; the README now says so out loud so the next reader does not "fix"
  it.
- **Not documented, deliberately:** the unconditional `--auth-token is not set`
  warning that `parseArgs()` prints on every terminal invocation (task-016's
  out-of-scope defect — documenting it would enshrine it), and the duplicated
  discovery-failure stderr line (by design, only visible when stderr is
  redirected).
- The architecture tree at the bottom of the README gained `src/terminal/` with
  all six sources; it had still shown `anoa-term (tools/anoa-term/)`. That block
  is easy to miss — it is 120 lines below the section everyone edits.

## task-018 — AGENTS.md corrected to the real stack (2026-08-01)

- **AGENTS.md was still the untouched Jonggrang scaffold**, top to bottom: Type
  `api`, Stack `node-typescript`, `kebab-case.ts` / `PascalCase.tsx` naming, a
  `routes/services/models` tree, `Framework: none`, `npm run db:migrate` in the
  setup block, and a TODO in every remaining section. Nothing in it had ever
  described this repo. Every agent session on this feature started from a file
  claiming the opposite of the truth — which is worth remembering when reading
  the earlier notes here: several of them re-derived facts (the port triplet, the
  ASCII-literal rule, the `-Wall` cleanliness) that a correct AGENTS.md would
  have handed over for free.
- **Scope widened deliberately, and it should have been.** The acceptance
  criteria name five sections; the file has nine, and the four unnamed ones
  (Naming Conventions, Code Patterns, Dependencies & Integrations, Development
  Setup) were the same node-typescript boilerplate. Correcting only the five
  would have left `Files: kebab-case.ts` sitting directly under a corrected
  `Stack: C++17 + Qt 6`, which is a worse failure mode than the original — a
  half-right document reads as authoritative. All nine sections are now real.
  Everything below `## Jonggrang Workflow` (workflow, bug reporting, task CLI,
  Jonggrang Notes) is tool documentation, not project knowledge, and was left
  alone.
- **Every claim was read off the source, not off this progress file.** The two
  differ in places and the source wins: the option help text came from
  `./build/anoa-browser terminal --help` on the live binary, the test commands
  from `Makefile` + `.github/workflows/ci.yml` + each `package.json`, the tree
  from `ls`, and the Qt component list from `CMakeLists.txt:36-42`. Where this
  file records a *rationale* (why `--term-*`, why `QCoreApplication`, why the
  pre-scan) that is what got lifted, because the code only shows the decision,
  not the reason.
- **Documentation validated by running what it documents**, which is the only
  validation a Markdown change admits. `make test QT_PREFIX=/opt/Qt/6.7.3/gcc_64`
  → 1/1 ctest (27 QTest cases) green; `ANOA_BINARY=../../build/anoa-browser npx
  vitest run` in `tests/integration` → 91/91 in 11 s; `anoa-browser terminal
  --help` lists all six terminal options with the documented ranges;
  `make lint` still prints "clang-tidy not found — skipping" (documented as
  skip-if-absent, so that is the accurate description). The sandbox toolchain
  from task-015 is still installed — `/opt/Qt/6.7.3` and `/usr/bin/cmake` — and
  `build/` was warm, so the whole check cost about a minute.
- **Three gotchas were promoted out of this file into AGENTS.md** because they
  are properties of the repo, not of this feature: the ASCII-only rule for
  `src/` string literals (task-001), the `::`-qualification rule for POSIX calls
  inside a `QObject` subclass (task-006), and the "check `\since` for any Qt API
  newer than 6.4" rule (task-015). The port triplet went too — it is the single
  most re-derived fact in this feature's history.
- **The `--help` consequence of the no-overloaded-flags decision is now written
  down**: both modes share one `QCommandLineParser`, so browser flags appear in
  `terminal --help` and terminal flags in the browser's. task-013 already found
  this the hard way when its `--gfx` grep turned out to prove less than it
  looked like it proved. Recorded next to the decision so the next reader does
  not treat the shared help output as a bug.
- **The unconditional `--auth-token is not set` warning is documented as known
  noise**, not as correct behaviour — the opposite of task-017's choice for the
  README, and deliberately so. A user-facing README that mentions it enshrines
  it; an agent-facing gotcha file that omits it lets the next agent spend an
  hour deciding whether it is a real defect. It is still unfixed and still
  unowned.

## Phase 10 — design verification (2026-08-01)

- **Verified against plan.md, not against the task notes.** Every Key Decision
  was checked at its implementation site: pre-scan + `QCoreApplication`
  (`main.cpp:26-61`), distinct `--term-*` names with browser `--port`/
  `--auth-token` unchanged (`config.cpp:174-196`), CLI-only terminal options
  (`loadConfigFile()` never touches them), `wss://` rejected in
  `validateCdpUrl()` with a `Q_ASSERT_X` backstop in `CdpClient`, inverted
  `deltaY = -dy` (`cdp_frame_backend.cpp:508`), CSS-pixel mapping via
  `viewportForImage()`, and a 14-entry named-key table that matches
  `anoa_browser.cpp:220-258` name-for-name.
- **The bash suites and `smoke.sh` fail in this sandbox for an environment
  reason, not a regression**: `wait_for_port()` uses `nc -z`, and netcat is not
  installed here (`curl` and `python3` are). The browser demonstrably starts —
  "DevTools listening" and "CdpProxy: listening" both appear before the FAIL.
  All three files are untouched by this branch (`git diff master...HEAD` on
  them is empty). Do not "fix" the binary in response to those failures.
- **What actually passes here**: `make test` → 1/1 ctest (27 QTest cases,
  including the three `QCoreApplication`-without-GUI checks); `npx vitest run`
  → 91/91 across 7 files, `terminal_cdp.test.js` 9/9; `make lint` skips
  (clang-tidy absent); `build-release-static/anoa-browser terminal --help`
  lists all six terminal options, so the static artifact does link the
  terminal sources.
- **The Windows path was verified negatively, as AGENTS.md requires**:
  `g++ -E -DQ_OS_WIN … src/main.cpp | grep -c runTerminal` → 0.
- **ci.yml grew a macOS unit-test matrix leg** that the plan asked for in words
  ("must be confirmed in CI on Linux and macOS, not assumed") but never listed
  under Affected Areas. Correct call; noting it so the file's diff is not read
  as scope creep later.
- **One requested capability is deliberately not shipped**: the planning Q&A
  asked for tabs and an in-terminal URL input line; plan.md moves both to Out
  of Scope with a reason (QtWebEngine has one `QWebEnginePage`, so
  `Target.createTarget` cannot work against anoa-browser's own CDP and the
  feature would ship asymmetric). `Page.navigate` exists in `CdpClient` as an
  unused primitive, which is the seam a follow-up feature would build on.

## 2026-08-01 — Phase 11 (domain-compliance): every mandatory pattern re-verified

All 13 AGENTS.md-mandated patterns pass. Two checks were previously "documented
but unverifiable"; both are now verifiable locally, and both recipes are below.

**The Qt 6.4 floor is now checkable locally — this was the real gap.**
AGENTS.md says "CI's 6.7.3 will not catch the regression" and there was no
local way to check. There is now:
    pip3 install --break-system-packages aqtinstall
    python3 -m aqt install-qt linux desktop 6.4.3 gcc_64 -m qtwebsockets \
        --outputdir /opt/Qt64
    g++ -fsyntax-only -std=c++17 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic \
        -I$Q -I$Q/QtCore -I$Q/QtGui -I$Q/QtNetwork -I$Q/QtWebSockets \
        -Isrc -Ibuild/anoa-browser_autogen/include <file>.cpp
No WebEngine module is needed: nothing under src/terminal/ includes it, so a
qtbase+qtwebsockets install (~fast) covers the entire new surface plus
config.cpp. All 6 files compile clean against 6.4.3.
This also compiles the `#if QT_VERSION >= QT_VERSION_CHECK(6,5,0)` ELSE branch
in cdp_client.cpp:105 — the deprecated `QOverload<>::of(&QWebSocket::error)`
path that CI at 6.7.3 never builds. It is clean, with no deprecation warning.
MUTATION-CHECKED (per the standing rule): a probe using `QWebSocket::error\
Occurred` is REJECTED by 6.4.3 and COMPILES on 6.7.3, so a green run is signal,
not a vacuous pass.

**The Windows negative check needs its includes shadowed, not just -DQ_OS_WIN.**
The AGENTS.md recipe `g++ -E -DQ_OS_WIN ... | grep -c runTerminal` FAILS on
Linux before it proves anything: real Qt headers pull QtGui/qwindowdefs_win.h
under Q_OS_WIN and preprocessing dies, so grep counts 0 on a dead file and the
check looks green while testing nothing. Copy main.cpp into a stub dir holding
empty QtGlobal/QApplication/QCoreApplication/QTextStream and empty
browser|cdp|http|config headers, then preprocess THAT (quoted includes resolve
next to the copied file, beating -Isrc). Give the stub terminal_app.h a unique
marker so you can grep the include as well as the symbol. Result, with a
control proving signal: Q_OS_WIN -> runTerminal 0 / marker 0 / windows-error 1;
no Q_OS_WIN -> runTerminal 2 / marker 1 / windows-error 0.

**Non-finding worth not re-deriving:** `./build/anoa-browser --help` prints 0
terminal flags and looks like a violation of the "both --help outputs list
every flag" decision. It is not — browser mode builds a QApplication, which
aborts with no DISPLAY before the parser ever runs. Use
`--headless --help` (the pre-scan sets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Then it is
6/6 terminal flags in browser help, and --port/--auth-token in terminal help.

**Everything else, all green:** ASCII-only string literals (checked inside
quoted literals only — the many non-ASCII hits under src/ are all comments,
which the rule allows); no unqualified connect/bind/listen/accept (`socket()`
at render_http_client.cpp:147 is unqualified and CORRECT — it has no QObject
collision); one add_executable; anoa-config-lib still config.cpp + Qt6::Core
alone; terminal options absent from loadConfigFile (lines 88-150) and handled
only inside parseArgs (151-291); 14 stderr+::exit(1) validations; terminal
runtime failure uses QCoreApplication::exit(1) (cdp_client.cpp:402) so termios
restore runs; no manual delete anywhere; no QEventLoop under src/terminal/ (the
seam is genuinely async); terminal_ui.* names no transport type; nothing
outside main.cpp/config.cpp touches argv; deltaY negation occurs exactly once,
at cdp_frame_backend.cpp:508. Full 17-TU rebuild from clean: 0 warnings under
-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic. ctest 1/1 passed.

**Naming non-issue:** grep flags bare fields in FrameData/DisplayMap/CdpResult/
Pending/Response. All are plain-data structs (incl. two nested inside QObject
classes), which follow the existing `Config` convention; the m_ rule is for
class members. No violation.

## 2026-08-01 — phase 13 test planning

- Wrote phase-13-test-plan.md. Existing coverage on this branch is real but narrow:
  14 QTest cases (config flags + the QCoreApplication/QImage assumption, now on a
  Linux+macOS matrix) and 9 vitest cases against the fake CDP endpoint.
- Biggest gap is not CDP: the DEFAULT /render/* backend in terminal mode has zero
  automated coverage. The plan's whole argument for shipping both backends was that
  HTTP is the known-good control — nothing tests the control. terminal_http.test.js
  is the P0 item.
- bug-001 (parsePpm size_t underflow) and bug-002 (split CSI escape) are both
  untestable today: parsePpm is a file-local static and processInput is private.
  Extracting pngDimensions/parsePpm into src/terminal/frame_bytes.{h,cpp} makes both
  testable AND removes the duplication in phase-12 finding #5 — one refactor, three
  payoffs. New unit targets must be SEPARATE from anoa-config-lib (AGENTS.md).
- Every pty-driven test is Linux-only (BSD script has no -e). macOS terminal-mode
  coverage is unit tests + non-pty CLI checks only. Say so in the phase-17 summary.
- The Windows compile-out check and the Qt 6.4 API floor check are both documented
  as verification steps in AGENTS.md and run in no job. Both are cheap CI steps.
- bug-001/bug-002 are still un-converted to tasks (jonggrang bug --feature cannot run
  non-interactively here). Convert before phase 14 or the regression tests have no
  owning fix.

## 2026-08-01 — phase 14 (testing)

Full write-up in phase-14-testing.md. What the next agent most needs to know:

- bug-001 and bug-002 are FIXED. Both were confirmed red against the pre-fix tree
  first: TERM-BYTES-02 failed its assertion, TERM-BYTES-03 took SIGSEGV and killed
  the test binary mid-run, and both bug-002 cases failed with the leaked bytes
  visible in the captured status bar. Do not treat them as open.
- The plan's TERM-BYTES-03 as written does NOT reproduce bug-001. "P6 4000 4000 255"
  plus ten bytes of body leaves pos inside the buffer, so the ordinary short-body
  check catches it. The body has to end exactly at the maxval — which is the
  reproducer bugs.md names. The committed case asserts both and says why.
- bug-003 is NEW and open: a /render/* peer that accepts and then sends nothing
  wedges the whole viewer, because the blocking read() now runs on the Qt event
  loop. Ctrl-C, SIGINT and SIGTERM are all ineffective; it needs SIGKILL, which
  skips atexit(restoreTerminal) and leaves the terminal in raw mode on the alt
  screen. THTTP-08 in terminal_http.test.js is committed as it.fails() and passes
  today BECAUSE of the wedge — it turns red when the fix lands, and that is the
  signal to delete it along with the bug.
- parsePpm() and pngDimensions() moved to src/terminal/frame_bytes.{h,cpp}, taking
  (const char *, size_t). The pngDimensions duplicate between the two backends is
  gone. Two new unit targets exist and are POSIX-only and Qt6::Core-only:
  anoa-terminal-bytes-lib and anoa-terminal-ui-lib. Never fold either into
  anoa-config-lib.
- TerminalUi is unit-testable without a terminal: construct it, never call begin(),
  and drive the public feedInput(). Skipping begin() is what keeps m_cols/m_rows at
  the 80x24 default, which is what makes the status-bar arithmetic a constant. Every
  such test redirects stdout to a temp file, and the capture object replays to
  stderr on failure — QTest's own logger writes to stdout, so without the replay a
  failing QVERIFY reports into the temp file and vanishes.
- The status bar's optional link field is NOT observable in the pty suites. At the
  harness's 100 columns the row is over budget before any link, so the link yields
  by design and is never painted. Assert on the wire there; the yielding rule is
  covered in the unit suite at 80 columns.
- The pty harness now lives in helpers.js (launchViewer, waitUntil, viewerErrors,
  sgrPress, TERM_COLS/ROWS/FPS). terminal_cdp.test.js and terminal_http.test.js
  share it; put new fake endpoints in the suites, not in helpers.
- Qt 6.4.3 installs in ~20 s for the floor check:
  aqt install-qt linux desktop 6.4.3 gcc_64 -m qtwebsockets -O /opt/Qt
  No WebEngine needed. src/terminal/*.cpp passes -fsyntax-only against it today.
- SANDBOX: nc is not installed here, and port_layout.test.sh's wait_for_port is
  built on `nc -z`, so its six PORT-* cases fail regardless of the binary. Baseline
  2 passed / 6 failed; unchanged by this phase. Do not chase them.
- SANDBOX: `jonggrang bug --feature <id>` still cannot file non-interactively — the
  global option parser eats --feature into WORK_FEATURE_ID before cmdBug() sees it.
  bugs.md also only understands [open] and [task:<id>]; there is no [fixed], and an
  unrecognised header is silently dropped from the parse. Resolved bugs stay [open]
  with RESOLVED as the first word of the body.
